rationale: Queuing the negative half of the parent configuration question, which the account has so far stated only from source: when the node's snapshot already covers the configuration change, a restart should recover the configuration in force. The probe runs the same remove-and-re-add history as the earlier stale-configuration cases but snapshots the node under test after the change and after further traffic, then restarts it from its stores. Local construction feedback shows the recovered configuration matching the configuration in force, so the trigger boundary is confirmed by measurement as well as by the scan arithmetic.

scope.description: A five-peer in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores, RestoreCommittedLogs and snapshotting disabled by configuration: two voters are removed, both are re-added, fifteen commands are committed, the node under test snapshots in that state, and it is then restarted from its stores. The probe reports the snapshot's index and configuration size, the configuration in force, the recovered configuration size and whether the two match.
assumptions: Cluster, transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
The snapshot is taken while the widened configuration is committed, so the snapshot records the configuration in force.
No bytes are altered outside the public snapshot, removal, addition and restart operations.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap five voters with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs=true; RemoveServer two voters and AddVoter them again through the retrying helper; apply fifteen commands; take a user snapshot on the node under test and record its index and configuration size together with the configuration in force; shut the node down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport; emit the event with the snapshot index, both configuration sizes, whether the recovered configuration matches the configuration in force and whether the gap is absent.
experiment.requirement: A node whose snapshot already covers a configuration change must recover the configuration in force on restart, whatever lies in its log below the commit index it recovers.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft establishes the recovered configuration from the snapshot and the log, and this probe names the boundary of the condition under which it fails.
